description: An underwriting manager must approve a receivables-backed revolving facility for a medical-supply distributor and finalize the commitment amount, equity condition, and security controls, with input from risk, legal, and relationship management.

shared_context.S1: The medical-supply distributor has requested a $12,000,000 revolving facility secured by trade receivables.
shared_context.S2: The preliminary underwriting model assumes an 80% advance rate and does not specify a required cash-equity contribution.
shared_context.S3: The facility would fund ordinary inventory purchases and customer deliveries, and the distributor's submitted financial statements show positive operating cash flow.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the binding underwriting decision. As part of the bank's normal approval huddle, risk, legal, and relationship management each give a review before Maya finalizes the terms.

PF1.text: Jonas confirmed this morning from the detailed receivables aging that policy-eligible receivables total exactly $9,000,000, and the applicable advance rate is 75%; he has not yet uploaded the revised borrowing-base worksheet to the credit file.

PF2.text: Elena found while reviewing the security documents this week that the bank must have a first-priority UCC filing before the first draw and a controlled lockbox for all facility collections; these requirements are not yet in the draft term sheet.

PF3.text: Ravi received a signed customer-side funding plan yesterday confirming that the distributor will contribute exactly $1,500,000 of cash equity before the first draw; the plan is still in his client file and has not been circulated to underwriting.

acceptance_conditions: The approved facility commitment must be exactly $6,750,000.
Exactly $1,500,000 of cash equity must be required before the first draw.
A first-priority UCC filing must be required before the first draw.
A controlled lockbox must be required for facility collections.
The settlement must include a borrowing-base commitment.

decisive_facts.why: The preliminary model would support the requested $12,000,000 facility without a revised borrowing-base control; PF1 changes the commitment to exactly $9,000,000 multiplied by 75%, or $6,750,000, and requires the borrowing-base certificate.
The draft terms contain neither security-perfection nor collection-control language; PF2 changes the settlement by requiring the UCC filing before the first draw and the controlled lockbox.

Without PF3, a cautious underwriting decision would not approve the facility because no first-loss funding is documented; PF3 changes the decision to approval conditioned on exactly $1,500,000 of cash equity before the first draw.
